title: Phishing Awareness
what: Phishing is a deceptive message designed to make someone disclose information, open an unexpected file, approve a request, or follow a misleading link.
why: A single rushed action can expose credentials or create a path for further investigation. Reporting early helps the security team protect others.
warning_signs: Unexpected sender or a look-alike display name
Urgency, secrecy, threats, or an unusual reward
Requests for passwords, MFA codes, payment, or sensitive data
Unexpected attachments, shortened links, or QR codes
safe_practices: Pause and inspect the sender and request
Use a known bookmark or official app instead of a message link
Verify payment or account changes through a separate trusted channel
Report suspicious messages using the approved process
if_something_happens: Do not reply or forward credentials. Report the message. If you interacted with it, contact the service desk/security team promptly and follow their instructions.
quick_task: Find your organization's approved phishing-reporting route.

title: Password Security
what: Password security means using unique, long authentication secrets and protecting them from reuse, disclosure, and insecure storage.
why: Password reuse lets one exposed password put multiple accounts at risk. Longer unique passwords make guessing and credential-stuffing less effective.
warning_signs: The same password is used on multiple services
A password is shared in chat, email, or a document
A login alert appears that you did not initiate
A password manager reports a reused or exposed secret
safe_practices: Use a reputable password manager approved for your environment
Create a unique long password or passphrase for each account
Never share passwords or one-time codes
Change a password if it may have been exposed, following policy
if_something_happens: Use a trusted device and official account recovery process, update the affected unique password, revoke unfamiliar sessions where supported, and report the event.
quick_task: Check one important account for password reuse without sharing the password.

title: MFA & Passkeys
what: Multi-factor authentication uses more than one proof of identity. Passkeys use public-key cryptography (commonly exposed through WebAuthn-compatible sign-in flows) and are designed to resist many credential-reuse and fake-site risks.
why: A password alone is a single factor. MFA adds a second check; phishing-resistant methods such as passkeys or security keys provide stronger protection when supported.
warning_signs: An MFA prompt arrives when you are not signing in
Someone asks you to read out an authentication code
Repeated prompts try to make you approve one
Recovery details changed unexpectedly
safe_practices: Enable MFA on important accounts
Prefer passkeys or security keys where available
Approve only sign-ins you initiated
Keep recovery methods current and protected
if_something_happens: Deny an unexpected request. Change the account password through the official site, review active sessions, and notify support/security.
quick_task: Review MFA options for one high-value account.

title: Social Engineering
what: Social engineering uses trust, authority, urgency, or helpfulness to influence a person into taking an unsafe action.
why: Technical controls cannot reliably distinguish every legitimate conversation from manipulation. Independent verification reduces pressure-based mistakes.
warning_signs: Requests to bypass normal approval or keep a task secret
Unexpected authority claims or unusual personal details
Pressure to transfer money, share data, or reset access immediately
A caller asks you to install tools or reveal a code
safe_practices: Slow down and follow normal approval steps
Verify requests using a directory number or known channel
Ask a colleague or manager through a separate channel
Share only the minimum information required
if_something_happens: Stop the interaction, retain relevant details, and report it through the approved security or fraud channel. Do not confront or investigate the requester yourself.
quick_task: Save a trusted contact route for reporting suspicious requests.

title: Safe Browsing
what: Safe browsing is using trusted sites, updates, and browser controls while limiting risky downloads, permissions, and credential entry.
why: Look-alike sites and unwanted downloads can put accounts or data at risk. A familiar logo is not proof that a page is authentic.
warning_signs: A link uses a misspelled or unexpected domain
A page asks for credentials after an unsolicited message
A download is unexpected or asks for excessive permissions
Browser security or certificate warnings appear
safe_practices: Use bookmarks or type a known official address
Keep browsers updated
Review permissions and avoid untrusted downloads
Stop if a warning appears; ask IT if unsure
if_something_happens: Close the page without entering more information, report an unexpected download, and contact support if credentials or data were submitted.
quick_task: Review browser updates and remove an extension you no longer need.

title: Secure Wi-Fi
what: Secure Wi-Fi habits reduce exposure when connecting devices to home, campus, or public wireless networks.
why: An unfamiliar network may be misconfigured or impersonate a legitimate hotspot. Network names alone do not prove who operates a network.
warning_signs: Two hotspots have similar names
A public hotspot unexpectedly asks for sensitive credentials
A connection requires installing an unknown certificate or profile
Sensitive work is being done on an untrusted device/network
safe_practices: Confirm the network name with staff through a trusted channel
Use your organization's approved secure access method
Keep device sharing disabled on public networks
Prefer mobile data for sensitive tasks when appropriate
if_something_happens: Disconnect from the network, forget it if advised by IT, and report unusual prompts or account activity.
quick_task: Disable automatic joining of unfamiliar open networks.

title: Software Updates
what: Software updates correct defects and may include security fixes for operating systems, browsers, apps, and devices.
why: Delayed updates can leave known weaknesses unaddressed. Organizations should prioritize updates using system criticality and exposure, not just a single severity number.
warning_signs: A device has missed repeated update reminders
An application is no longer supported
An update prompt appears from an untrusted pop-up
A critical work app is far behind its managed version
safe_practices: Use approved update channels
Enable managed automatic updates where appropriate
Restart when updates require it
Report devices that cannot update
if_something_happens: Do not install software from a pop-up. Use the official update mechanism or contact IT for managed systems.
quick_task: Check that one personal device is set to receive security updates.

title: Ransomware Awareness
what: Ransomware is a category of harmful activity that can encrypt files, disrupt services, create operational downtime, and may involve data theft or extortion. This module stays at a defensive awareness level.
why: Recovery may be operationally difficult and time-sensitive. Preparation, backups, least privilege, monitoring, and practiced response reduce impact.
warning_signs: Unexpected file access or extension changes
Security tools report unusual activity
A device shows an unexpected demand or service disruption
Multiple systems become unavailable at once
safe_practices: Maintain tested, protected backups
Use MFA and least privilege
Keep managed systems updated
Report unusual endpoint behavior promptly
if_something_happens: Stop using the affected device and contact your security/IT incident channel immediately. Preserve the message and follow approved response instructions; do not attempt ad-hoc cleanup.
quick_task: Learn where your team's incident-response contact and backup guidance are documented.

title: USB & Removable Media
what: Removable media can move data between systems and may also introduce untrusted files or unexpected device behavior.
why: Unknown media can bypass normal sharing controls or expose confidential information when misplaced.
warning_signs: A found or gifted drive has no clear owner
A device prompts you to run or install something
Sensitive information is copied to unapproved media
A drive is unexpectedly left connected
safe_practices: Use organization-approved encrypted media only
Do not plug in found devices
Follow data-transfer and handling policy
Return or report lost media promptly
if_something_happens: Disconnect the media if safe to do so, do not open or execute content, and contact IT/security for guidance.

title: Data Privacy
what: Data privacy is responsible collection, use, storage, and sharing of information, especially personal, sensitive, or confidential data.
why: Unnecessary collection and oversharing increase the impact of mistakes and make data harder to protect.
warning_signs: A request asks for more personal data than the task needs
Information is sent to an unintended recipient
Sensitive data is stored in an unapproved location
Screens or printouts expose information to others
safe_practices: Apply data-minimization principles
Check recipients and sharing permissions
Use approved storage and retention settings
Lock devices and protect printed records
if_something_happens: Report a suspected disclosure promptly using privacy/security procedures. Include what was shared, when, and with whom, without forwarding sensitive content unnecessarily.
quick_task: Review sharing permissions on one document you own.

title: Mobile Security
what: Mobile security protects phones and tablets that hold work accounts, messages, or sensitive information.
why: A lost or unlocked device can expose accounts and communications. Mobile devices also need timely updates and managed access controls.
warning_signs: A device is lost or stolen
An app requests unexpected access to contacts, camera, or files
A sign-in prompt appears after a device handoff
A device is no longer receiving security updates
safe_practices: Use a strong screen lock and supported biometrics
Install apps only from trusted stores and approved catalogs
Keep the device updated
Report loss quickly so approved protections can be applied
if_something_happens: Contact your service desk/security team immediately and use only approved device-recovery steps. Change affected account credentials if directed.
quick_task: Turn on automatic screen locking and review app permissions.

title: Remote Work Security
what: Remote-work security applies safe access, privacy, and device practices outside a managed office.
why: Work can happen on varied networks and in shared spaces, making physical privacy and trusted connectivity important.
warning_signs: A device is shared with an untrusted user
A video call or screen exposes confidential information
A request asks you to bypass approved remote access
A device is left unattended in a public area
safe_practices: Use organization-approved devices and access methods
Lock screens when stepping away
Keep sensitive conversations private
Report lost devices or access issues quickly
if_something_happens: Disconnect from an untrusted session if safe, contact IT/security, and follow approved incident guidance.
quick_task: Set a short automatic screen-lock timeout on your work device.

title: Cloud Account Security
what: Cloud-account security protects identities, sharing settings, and access to hosted services and stored data.
why: A compromised account or overly broad sharing permission can expose information across many devices and collaborators.
warning_signs: Unfamiliar sign-in or session notification
Unexpected file-sharing invitation or permission change
MFA prompts you did not start
New connected app or recovery method you do not recognize
safe_practices: Use unique credentials and MFA/passkeys
Review sharing links and connected applications
Use least-privilege access
Report unusual sessions instead of ignoring alerts
if_something_happens: Use the service's official security page from a trusted route, revoke unfamiliar sessions if policy allows, and notify the account owner/security team.
quick_task: Review active sessions and shared links for one cloud account.

title: Incident Reporting
what: Incident reporting is promptly sharing a suspected security event with the designated team so it can assess and coordinate a response.
why: Early, accurate reporting can limit delay and preserve context. Reporting a suspicion does not mean the reporter is at fault.
warning_signs: You clicked an unexpected link or shared information
A device behaves unusually
A sign-in alert is unfamiliar
A suspicious request reached you or a colleague
safe_practices: Use the approved security/service-desk channel
Record time, device, and what happened
Do not delete or alter relevant evidence unless instructed
Be factual; label assumptions as assumptions
if_something_happens: Report promptly, include what you observed and actions already taken, and follow guidance from the response team.
quick_task: Bookmark the incident-reporting contact or portal.

title: AI-Enabled Scam Awareness
what: AI-enabled scams may use generated text, images, or voice to imitate people or create convincing messages. A polished message is not proof of authenticity.
why: Synthetic media can make impersonation more persuasive, while urgency and unusual requests remain useful warning signs.
warning_signs: An urgent request for money, gift cards, codes, or data
A familiar voice asks for an unusual exception
Small inconsistencies in context, names, or process
Pressure to bypass normal verification
safe_practices: Verify sensitive requests through a second trusted channel
Use agreed confirmation phrases only if your organization has a policy
Follow payment and identity-verification procedures
Report suspected impersonation
if_something_happens: Pause the transaction or disclosure, verify independently, and report the attempt through security or fraud channels.
quick_task: Agree on a trusted callback method for sensitive requests.
